A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AMPNet and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables. The comparison includes v2 Appendix A.1–A.5; v1 ends with references and contains no appendix. The substantial revision does not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original AMPNet Cora accuracy, cellular-automata transition-attention results, and gene/word attention visualizations in Section 4. The reused GCN/GAT baseline scores are distinguishable from these original results.

after.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction, link-prediction, and node-classification results in Tables 1–4, plus biological and word-attention case studies in Section 5 and Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: The cross-node attention mechanism remains, but the reported update changes from direct aggregation in v1 Equation 1 to a learned combination of previous node features and aggregated messages in v2 Equation 6. v2 also changes mouse-gene embeddings from principal components to learned vectors and introduces patch/positional encodings and a masked-image encoder–decoder, extending v1's two-layer classification setup.

E1.justification: v2 adds UK Biobank fMRI reconstruction, human-heart gene-expression prediction, OGBN-arXiv link prediction, CIFAR-100 image-network reconstruction, and Pubmed/Amazon Computers node classification. Cora and mouse hippocampus remain, but mouse evaluation changes to masked gene-expression prediction. The six-color cellular-automata next-state benchmark is removed.

E2.justification: Cora's MLP/GCN/GAT comparison in v1 Table 2 is replaced by DGI, GRACE, BGRL, GraphMAE, and feature/graph/random-initialization controls in v2 Table 4. New reconstruction comparisons include GraphSAGE and GraphMAE, with GPS Graph Transformer evaluated on fMRI only. One comparator's identity remains ambiguous: Table 4 names DeepWalk, whereas Appendix A.3 describes node2vec.

E3.justification: Cora changes from supervised classification to unsupervised representation learning followed by linear-classifier evaluation in v2 Appendix A.3. New experiments introduce 50% fMRI masking with three baseline imputation strategies, 20% gene/image masking, patch-based reconstruction, and separately constructed CIFAR training/validation/test graphs. v2 also introduces per-task hyperparameter searches and a stated model-capacity matching procedure.

E4.justification: v2 adds a positional-encoding ablation for fMRI, age/PTSD attention analyses, an astrocyte attention and gene-embedding UMAP study, and interpretable word-attention analysis on OGBN-arXiv. These replace or extend v1's gene/Cora heatmap analyses. The controlled cellular-automata test of attention against known transition rules is removed.

E5.justification: v1 provides no run counts or uncertainty for its own AMPNet results; its GAT uncertainty is borrowed from prior work. v2 Tables 1–2 and Appendix A.3 specify five runs, and Tables 1–4 report plus/minus quantities for AMPNet and comparators. The PDFs do not establish an increase from a known earlier run count, and v2 does not define whether the plus/minus quantities are standard deviations or standard errors.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive numerical results, including AMPNet fMRI R2 of 0.578 with positional encoding and OGBN-arXiv AUROC of 89.5 ± 0.13. Cora's 82.3% in v1 becomes 73.0 ± 3.10 in v2 under a different evaluation protocol, so this is not a comparable performance decline. The cellular-automata attention results of 0.97–1.00 and the original gene/Cora heatmap findings are removed.

T1.justification: The scaled-dot-product attention formula is retained, but v2 Equation 6 adds a formal definition combining the previous node representation with the neighborhood aggregate through learned weights. This is a limited mathematical extension; neither version supplies theorems or proofs. The removed delay-differential-operator discussion is conceptual rather than a lost proof.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes interpretable message passing, comparable Cora performance, and recovery of cellular-automata rules. v2 makes rich feature representation and superior self-supervised prediction central contributions, including explicit fMRI benefits attributed to positional encoding. The cellular-automata recovery contribution disappears from the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds the qualification that attention weights are not completely faithful explanations, new biological interpretations of fMRI and astrocyte attention, and an argument that AMPNet is better suited to richly annotated features than ordinary bag-of-words benchmarks. v1's delay-differential/PDE interpretation and MOBP–Cryab discussion are removed. The future directions concerning sparse attention, feature selection, and edge features largely remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1–A.5 adds concrete preprocessing, splits, graph-construction probabilities, tokenization/masking specifications, GPU memory information, and per-model parameter counts and training hyperparameters in Tables 5–7. This substantially expands v1's sampling descriptions and brief training setup. Conversely, v1's explicit Adam optimizer and four-attention-head disclosures are not retained.

R1.justification: v1's extensive cellular-automata/PDE positioning is removed. v2 expands related work into post-hoc explanation and interpretable-modeling categories, adding GraphLIME, attention-faithfulness debates, and other explanation methods. GraphMAE, GPS, masked image autoencoders, and additional biological literature establish substantially different empirical and conceptual positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Feature embedding now precedes message creation, interpretability receives a dedicated section, and dataset details, training information, and node-classification reporting are organized into Appendix A. Citation style and the author/affiliation presentation also change.

P2.justification: The framework diagram is redrawn as a multipanel overview, and the cellular-automata diagram is replaced by fMRI/genomics/image graph-construction schematics. Interpretability displays are replaced or expanded with age/PTSD heatmaps, astrocyte attention and UMAP, and word-attention panels. v2 also adds algorithm pseudocode, multi-metric benchmark tables, hyperparameter tables, and substantially reformats the page layout.

improvement.justification: v1's comparative predictive evidence largely rests on one Cora accuracy table. v2 substantially strengthens that evidence through reconstruction and link-prediction comparisons, a positional-encoding ablation, repeated-run reporting, and detailed experimental specifications. Removing the known-rule cellular-automata test weakens direct interpretability validation, and the broad superiority claim overstates Appendix Table 4, where AMPNet does not lead on Cora or Amazon Computers. Nevertheless, the gains in empirical support and reproducibility constitute a substantial overall improvement.
